title: Streaming ACK Flood — Autopsy and Runbook Draft
impact: Multiple hosted-api customers experienced mass streaming session resets and elevated tail latency for streaming endpoints across us-west-1 and eu-central-1 during the 2029-03-14 22:10–23:05 UTC window. ~12% of active streaming sessions saw one or more abrupt disconnects; transient 5xx rate increased to 4.8% service-wide. No data loss reported but user-facing UX (chat apps) degraded noticeably.
detection: SRE alert: streaming-session-error-rate spike at 22:12 UTC (alert threshold = 0.8%), oncall paged. Oncall performed initial triage via dashboards (streaming-connects, ttfb, reconnects) and correlated with edge TCP metrics showing connection churn and unusually high ACK traffic from a set of client IP CIDRs.
timeline:
22:10 — first metric drift (streaming reconnects) observed in us-west-1
22:12 — Pager: streaming-error-rate > threshold; SRE oncall (Aisha) triages
22:16 — Identified concentrated ACK bursts from ~8 client ASN blocks; connections on edge proxies showing repeated short RTTs and rehandshakes
22:24 — Temporary mitigation: enable per-edge aggressive backoff (conn-level accept throttle) and widen multiplex pool; reconnect rate drops but some sessions still fail
22:35 — Confirmed correlation with a client rollout (third-party SDK v2.3.0) releasing 'aggressive-acks' optimization via Slack & partner contact
22:46 — Deployed server-side ACK-coalescing heuristic (edge config change) as a stopgap; immediate improvement in tail latency and reconnects
23:02 — Rolling rollback of partner-swift SDK observed (partner confirmed rollback at 22:55 UTC)
23:05 — System stabilized; alerts cleared. Post-incident monitoring continued for 24h.
root_cause: A confluence of factors: (1) a client SDK release (partner SDK v2.3.0) introduced an optimization that sent tight ACK bursts on multiplexed streaming connections to improve client-side p99 latency; (2) our edge multiplexing + connection reuse assumptions didn't account for sustained high-rate ACK bursts from many clients sharing a small number of transport connections, which triggered connection rehandshakes and evicted ephemeral session state (KV caches, session leases); (3) the eviction and re-connect pattern created thrashing that pushed some internal buffers into overload, causing retries and a small but service-wide 5xx amplification. In short: client behavior that looked benign per-connection but is pathological when many clients share multiplexed connections combined with edge resource pressure and insufficient ACK-coalescing on the server path.
mitigation_performed:
- Immediate: enabled per-edge connection acceptance backoff (short-term throttle) and widened multiplex pool config to reduce hot-connection contention.
- Stopgap: rolled out an ACK-coalescing heuristic at the edge layer (aggregate rapid ACKs within 10ms into a single processed event).
- Coordination: contacted partner to request rollback of the SDK feature; partner performed rollback at 22:55 UTC.
- Monitoring: raised streaming reconnect and ack-rate alerts and instrumented a temporary per-client ack-rate dashboard.
postmortem_notes:
- This incident differs from prior streaming failures (which were often server-side KV-lock cascades) because the dominant trigger originated from valid client TCP-level behavior that interacts poorly with multiplexing.
- Existing runbooks assumed client ACK patterns are low-entropy; that assumption is false for some third-party SDKs.
- Our telemetry lacked a concise per-connection ack-rate signal; we inferred the pattern from edge packet counters and correlating IPs.

runbook_draft:
Trigger conditions:
- streaming-error-rate > 1% AND reconnect-rate > 0.5% within 5m OR ack-rate per-edge > threshold
Immediate steps:
1) Identify top offending client IP blocks via ack-rate dashboard.
2) Apply per-edge connection acceptance backoff for affected proxies (knobs: accept-throttle-ms, max-new-per-sec).
3) If immediate effect not observed, enable ack-coalescing heuristic on affected edge pools.
4) Notify partner(s) and request rollback or SDK throttle.
Mitigations to avoid customer impact:
- Prefer server-side coalescing before dropping connections.
- Expand multiplex pool to avoid too many clients multiplexing onto a single ephemeral conn.
Follow-up investigation:
- Correlate KV cache eviction spikes with connection churn.
- Validate no lingering client retries causing downstream overload.
Escalation:
- If 5xx > 5% or reconnects persist > 30 minutes after heuristics, page eng-serving-runtime leads and on-call infra.
